newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish group seeking PBK stake to wait for IPO.
newsitem.headline: Polish group seeking PBK stake to wait for IPO.

text.p: A consortium of three Polish banks and an insurer which bid in the cancelled tender for Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) may buy shares in its planned public offer, Polish Development Bank (PBR) said.
PBR had bid with Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA (BPH), Kredyt Bank and Warta for up to 65 percent of PBK but on Tuesday the government decided to sell at least 51 percent in a public offering.
South Korea's Samsung Group was also bidding.

"A new public-offering conception of PBK's privatisation will be announced. Then a decision will also be taken on the participation of the Polish banking-insurance group in PBK's privatisation's new form," PBR said in a Wednesday statement.

Under the original privatisation plan only 15 percent of PBK was to be sold in a public offering, expected in the fourth quarter of this year, with 65 percent earmarked for a strategic investor or a consortium and the rest set aside for the bank's employees and a special reserve for restitution claims.

The decision on the choice of the strategic investor had been delayed for months and Samsung earlier this month accused the Polish government of favouring the Polish offer even though it was less attractive financially.

Warsaw-based PBK is one of Poland's leading retail banks. HSBC Investment Services SA, which advised the government on the bank's privatisation, has estimated its value at between 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys ($420 million-$500 million).
